422.t: Jazz today: Newark partnerships and the museum-music fear

But he used to talk about the fact that we have this chancellor…

422.t: Jazz parties, documentaries, 'jazz is dead' and closing
422.s: They discuss declining jazz parties, new films, why jazz is declared dead, and close optimistically.
422.q: That’s a shame. And I don’t know about the jazz cruises. I don’t know if they’re still happening or not. I suppose once in a while.

422.t: Valery Ponomarev and the NJPAC teens: the future of jazz
422.s: Seeing teens play jazz convinces him jazz has a future, though never popular as in the 30s and 40s.
422.q: They have a thing called jazz for teens. And they have these kids come in, and he is instructing them how to play jazz. 373.t: Why there is no serious American jazz magazine

373.ch: Jazz journalism and the music today

There are others. I understand there’s a good one in Poland. In England they have two or three ones, not…

373.t: The state of jazz journalism and critics: Friedwald, Crouch, black press
373.s: Asked about jazz journalism, he praises Will Friedwald and Stanley Crouch, laments the lack of black writers and discusses the black press's neglect.
373.ch: Jazz journalism and the music today
373.q: Like everything else, it’s a mixed situation. There was a time when there were very few people writing about it. I mentioned some of the early ones who were very important, like Charles Edward Smith. In terms of what’s happening now, there’s one kind that’s very important, certainly to musicians,…

860.t: Future of British traditional jazz and current audiences
860.s: The amateur and semi-professional scene is lively and improving; Colyer says audiences fluctuate but he has a staunch following in Britain and Germany. The transcript ends with ASR repetition.

456.t: Will New Orleans-style and brass band jazz survive?

1001.t: Where jazz is headed and building an audience

358.t: Teenagers with money and the generation gap
358.s: Working mothers in wartime gave kids money, advertising shifted to youth and parents lost authority.
358.q: when the mothers did not come back home after working in the plants in the Second World War, they had money. So after the war was over they had this — we had no mothers at home.

813.t: Worries about the future audience for pre-bebop jazz
